messages:
maria: quick heads-up — I'm prototyping a 'Querybook' flow to let product teams save per-route/per-model queries and surface routing + quota hints in the console. want to align API + UX before i ship the mockups :wave:

alex: +1 on the feature. couple of constraints: list view must stay cheap. we should avoid computing full quota previews for every row at render time. maybe an on-demand preview panel? :thinking:

devon: agree. telemetry sampling makes estimation noisy anyway. suggestion: show a lightweight estimate (median token burn last 7d) and a detailed modal that does a live calc when user clicks "Quota preview". cheap default in list, heavier calc on demand.

kai: API question: do we store routing hints (pinned_model, fallbacks) on the saved-query resource, or compute routing by evaluating the route at read-time? storing them makes rollback/trace easier but can drift if model mapping changes. server-side evaluation ensures correctness but makes the saved-query opaque.

alex: my vote = store an explicit snapshot of routing decisions (pinned_model + fallback list + routing_policy_version) on save. UX needs reproducibility for audits. we can include a server-side validation step that flags stale pins.

maria: +1 for reproducibility. auditability is critical for enterprise customers. but we should minimize surface area for accidental stale pins — maybe show a small badge when the pinned_model is no longer in the catalog.

devon: telemetry concern: if we expose per-query quota estimates we must make it clear these are estimates (sampling / batching differences). add a tooltip and a link to Logs/Tasks for the exact calc.

kai: rollout UX: if we add a new field to saved-query API (routing_hint), how do we migrate older saved queries? do we backfill by hitting the routing service (expensive) or leave null and compute on read?

alex: Migration plan idea: backfill async in background for high-usage saved-queries only. add a feature-flagged migration job. default read-time fallback is server-eval if snapshot missing.

maria: sounds reasonable. smaller teams won't notice lag. enterprise customers can request a full backfill as part of onboarding.

sam-bot: deploy-bot: CI green for PR #4256 (api: saved-query routing_hint + pinned_model). auto-run integration tests: passed. :white_check_mark:

devon: quick API shape proposal (rough):
```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "query": "string",
  "scope": {"route_ids": ["r123"]},
  "snapshot": {
    "pinned_model": "redwood-7b-q4",
    "fallbacks": ["redwood-3b-q4"],
    "routing_policy_version": "v2"
  },
  "ui_prefs": {"show_quota_preview": true}
}
```

alex: that's pretty much what i had in mind. minor nit: prefer `routing_policy_ref` instead of version string so we can map to policy metadata (region, tier).

kai: also we need to decide where to compute cheap quota estimate. propose `analytics-service` produces an estimate cached on the saved-query document under `estimates.cache_7d`. reads hit the cache, detailed modal calls `estimates/recalculate` endpoint.

maria: ok action items: (1) alex -> open API PR to add `snapshot` + `routing_policy_ref` (2) kai -> design migration job and cheap cache endpoint sketch (3) devon -> copy for tooltip + telemetry caveats in console mockups (4) i'll put a short spec in the weekly product sync.

alex: i'll spin the PR today, will include the `stale_pin` flag and a lightweight `estimated_tokens` property schema.

devon: UX note: in the saved-query list, show a small flame icon for high-cost queries and hover to show top contributing model/token assumptions. keeps list useful at glance.

maria: love that. add to spec. final question — for canary rollouts of the console change, do we gate by org-level feature flags or rollout by %?

kai: org-level flags for enterprise, % rollout for public. console already supports per-org feature gates, so reuse that.

maria: perfect — thanks all. i'll update the spec and tag you on the PRs.

alex: thumbs up, ping me if you want me to pair on the migration job.

sam-bot: reminder: weekly-api-standup 2pm today, adding this to the agenda.
